0: Cold open of a 7-minute animated explainer for adults, like a calm, slightly amused airline insider letting you in on secrets. Start INSTANTLY, no breath: a low, intriguing 'Right before some planes land at night, the crew switches the cabin lights off.' then a deadpan beat 'On purpose.' Line 2 a raised-stakes, serious tone on 'in case you have to get out, fast.' Line 3 friendly and inviting, like boarding with a friend. Then clear, relaxed storytelling about the left door; a light smile on 'the right side is busy'; warm and easy on the last line about your phone.
1: Crisp and curious on 'Airplane mode.' Gently myth-busting on the first fact, careful and precise on 'never proven'. Clear explainer on the towers and 1991. Intriguing and a little playful on the mosquito buzz in the headsets. Serious, measured on takeoff and landing. Thoughtful on 'the one time it might', then a light hand-off line.
2: Brisk list rhythm on 'Seat back upright. Tray table up.' A dramatic, slower beat on 'Ninety seconds.' Clear and impressed on the certification test. Real amazement on the A380 numbers, with weight on 'seventy-eight seconds'. Vivid and practical on 'picture your row'. Serious on the accidents line. Then a curious, inviting hand-off to the tiny hole.
3: Intrigued on 'That tiny hole.' Reassuring on 'It's there on purpose.' Clear, satisfying explainer on the three panes, with a tiny smile on 'fingers and scratches'. Strong on 'pushes outward, hard.' Calm and satisfying on the middle pane resting. Light on the fog. Then a comic, suspicious pause before 'strange'.
4: Wry and amused on 'Food on a plane tastes bland.' A playful turn on 'It's you.' Clear storytelling on the Lufthansa and Fraunhofer test. Precise on the percentages. Fascinated on smell being most of flavour. A bright little reveal on umami and tomatoes, amused on the tomato juice habit. Then a slower, slightly serious hand-off to the safety card.
5: Natural, conversational read, like quietly telling one friend something important on a plane: no announcer tone, natural pauses, varied pace. Calm and caring on the rule, gentle on 'Even your own child.' Thoughtful on 'It's actually the opposite.' Slower and sobering on thirty seconds to a minute; say 'time of useful consciousness' plainly. Soft, a little eerie on 'you don't feel it coming'. Warm and reassuring on 'all the time you need to help them', steady on the descent, a soft hand-off to the lights.
6: Natural, conversational read to one friend, no announcer tone, natural pauses and varied pace. Knowing on 'The one from the start.' Relaxed and clear on the lights and shades, relatable on walking into a dark room, satisfied on 'Your eyes are already ready.' Then an easy, unhurried recap of the seven (not a list shout), a friendly real question for the comments, and the last line dry and warm with a real pause before 'you'll know'.
